explain.good_summary: In this sample report, 2 results are within the printed range: RBC, Platelets.
explain.concern_summary: 7 results are outside the printed range: Hemoglobin, WBC, MCV, Fasting Glucose, ALT (SGPT), Total Cholesterol, Vitamin D. This is a made-up sample, but on a real report you should talk to a doctor about any result outside its range.
doctor_points: Which of the results outside the range matter most for me?
Do any of these need a repeat test?
Could my diet, medicines or a recent illness explain these results?

explanations.0: This test measures the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body. This result is low compared with the printed range. A low result can be linked to iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, blood loss, or long-term illness. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.1: This test measures the number of red blood cells, which carry oxygen. This result is within the printed range.
explanations.2: This test measures the number of white blood cells, which fight infection. This result is high compared with the printed range. A high result can be linked to infection, inflammation, stress, smoking or some medicines. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.3: This test measures tiny cell pieces that help blood clot. This result is within the printed range.
explanations.4: This test measures the average size of your red blood cells. This result is low compared with the printed range. A low result can be linked to small red cells, often with iron deficiency. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.5: This test measures the amount of sugar in your blood. This result is high compared with the printed range. A high result can be linked to eating before a fasting test, stress, infection, or diabetes or pre-diabetes. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.6: This test measures an enzyme found mostly in the liver that leaks into the blood when liver cells are irritated. This result is high compared with the printed range. A high result can be linked to fatty liver, alcohol, some medicines, viral infections of the liver or other liver irritation. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.7: This test measures the total amount of cholesterol, a fatty substance, in your blood. This result is high compared with the printed range. A high result can be linked to a diet high in saturated fat, little exercise, family history, or thyroid and kidney conditions. Ask your doctor what it means for you.
explanations.8: This test measures the level of vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium for bones. This result is low compared with the printed range. A low result can be linked to little sun exposure, diet, darker skin, or absorption problems. Ask your doctor what it means for you.

explain.spoken_english: This is a sample report. Some results are inside the printed range and some are outside it. For any result outside the range, please talk to a doctor.
